exposure: introduction of SPEED clinical pathway for postpartum hemorrhage management
outcome: hemoglobin levels upon emergency room arrival
hematocrit values upon emergency room arrival
vital signs upon emergency room arrival
duration until treatment by obstetricians and gynecologists
duration between chest radiography ordering and performance
duration until transfusion of cross-matched red blood cells
cohort: The study included 229 patients experiencing postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), divided into a non-SPEED group (74 patients treated before the protocol introduction) and a SPEED group (155 patients treated after the protocol introduction).
finding: The SPEED clinical pathway significantly reduced turnaround time for hemoglobin, time to treatment by obstetricians and gynecologists, time between chest radiography ordering and performance, and time until transfusion of cross-matched red blood cells, while increasing the uterus preservation rate.
